layer1_identification.broadClassification: food prop / stylized low-poly game asset
layer1_identification.note: Same style family as campagne/pancake. assets/prompts/breads/wholewheat.json explicitly calls this 'the same silhouette family as a campagne boule', but the rendered reference is measurably rounder/taller (see below) - per CRIB, the image is the authority on proportions, the JSON only on color, so this bread's own DOME_HEIGHT is measured independently while the ring-groove/wobble code is shared with campagne via scripts/breads/domeShell.ts.

layer2_form_silhouette.boundingVolume: rounder, taller dome than campagne - closer to a squashed sphere
layer2_form_silhouette.symmetry: radial about the vertical axis, no slash to break it (unlike campagne)
layer2_form_silhouette.shapeLanguage: organic dome expressed with geometric faceting

measurements_px.topdown_ring_count: approximately 12-13 concentric rings, denser and covering nearly the full visible disk edge-to-edge (no smooth outer margin, unlike campagne's early groove-zone mistake)

macro: dome body (single continuous boule, no slash)
micro: concentric banneton ring grooves across the whole dome surface
coarse whole-grain speckle across the crust

layer4_spatial: <ring grooves, embedded-in, dome body> contact: concentric shallow grooves, centered on the apex, covering the whole visible dome surface edge to edge
<speckle flecks, scattered-on, dome surface> contact: small raised/light flecks scattered densely and fairly uniformly (not ridge-biased like campagne's flour dust)
no floating parts; single continuous body resting on a flat unseen base, no slash/crumb split

layer5_materials.single_substance: opaque dielectric, matte crust only - no second material (no slash exposes any crumb)
layer5_materials.roughness: 1.0 (fully matte clay); no specular lobe anywhere
layer5_materials.relief: faceted planar shading; ring grooves read as shallow concentric channels, speckle reads as small faceted flecks
layer5_materials.runtimeNote: consumer runtime force-replaces every material with MeshLambertMaterial keeping only map and color (scripts/breads/types.ts section 2)

layer6_color.crustBase: #8C5A32 - JSON states this is 'one full shade darker than a plain campagne crust' (campagne is #A9713F)
layer6_color.speckleFleck: not specified in JSON hex - resolved as a documented deterministic lighten of the crust base (see author_spec.py), distinct from campagne's flour-dust hex since this is grain fleck, not surface dusting

layer7_identity_features: spiral/concentric banneton ring markings pressed across the whole top surface, denser than campagne's and reaching edge to edge
coarse grainy speckle suggesting whole-grain flecks across the whole crust - the second identity marker alongside the darker base tone
one full shade darker crust than campagne - assets/prompts/breads/wholewheat.json notes_ko: without this the model would read as plain white bread
no slash, no cross pattern - a plain unbroken dome unlike campagne
layer8_uncertainty: underside is never visible in any of the three views or any turntable azimuth above the horizon - modelled as a flat closed base
exact ring phase/spiral pitch and exact speckle positions are not identity-critical; ring count/coverage and speckle density/color are what is matched
speckle fleck hex has no source in the prompt JSON; resolved by a documented deterministic lighten of the crust base, never pixel-sampled (types.ts section 8)
